Q: Can the LinkedIn API return a list of a user's saved articles? A:

Update, 2026: this is still not possible with an official API. Saved articles and saved posts have never been exposed by LinkedIn's APIs. The current Marketing and Community Management APIs do not include saved items, and the q=authors finder mentioned in the earlier answer only returns articles published by a member, not the ones they saved.

Two practical routes, depending on what you need:

1. Official data export (no code, links only). Settings > Data Privacy > Get a copy of your data, then select "Saved items". LinkedIn emails you a CSV containing the saved post URLs and save dates, and nothing else: no post text, no author, no media. Usable as a backup of links, not enough to build a feature on.

2. Capture from your own logged-in session. The saved-posts data is only rendered at linkedin.com/my-items/saved-posts/ for the member themselves, so tools in this space work by capturing posts from your own browser session (usually a browser extension) and then exposing them over a proper API. Disclosure: I am the founder of LinkedMash, which works exactly this way: a Chrome extension imports your saved posts, and you then get a REST API and an MCP server over your own library. Other capture-based tools exist as well; none of them can use an official API because there is none.

If you only need your own saved items occasionally, the export CSV plus re-fetching each URL can be enough, but note that LinkedIn aggressively rate-limits and login-walls those fetches.

Q: Dispatcher.__init__() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given A:

The Dispatcher.__init__() you were trying to call was documented here.

def __init__(self, *, storage: BaseStorage | None = None, fsm_strategy: FSMStrategy = FSMStrategy.USER_IN_CHAT, events_isolation: BaseEventIsolation | None = None, disable_fsm: bool = False, name: str | None = None, **kwargs: Any)

It does not take any positional arguments (you need to specify the options using keyword arguments. The one argument you are seeing is actually the self argument, which refers to the class itself and you do not really need to care about it.

The actual way to do what you was trying to do was also documented at the bottom of the in Handling Updates.

bot = Bot(...)
dp = Dispathcher()

...

result = await dp.feed_update(bot=bot, update=incoming_update)

Q: npm install gifsicle behind corporate proxy failed or stuck at windows system A:

I've faced similar issue not exactly same.npm install command for most of the packages. I am behind corporate proxy. For this i tried many solutions it never worked. Finally i did this,

Try to run the following command in cmd, npm config set https-proxy "http://your_companyproxy_here:8080"

Then it will work fine.

Q: Update List of entities in one query jpa A:

Looks like you miss where keyword

update Parent p set p.children=:childrenwhere where p in (:parents)

or you can try with id

update Parent p set p.children=:childrenwhere where p.id in (:parentIds)
